title: add-rbacv2-temporal-revocation-webhook-and-region-pinned-kms-attribution
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Customers with strict compliance requirements have asked for enforcement of timebound RBAC grants plus clear attribution of KMS usage when region-pin policies are in effect. This PR introduces a lightweight RBACv2 admission webhook that enforces grant revocation/time-to-live semantics at decision time, plus a KMS Usage Attributor that tags KMS calls with operator identity, grant-id and region-pin provenance and emits attribution metrics and audit events. Motivation: reduce silent policy drift (expired grants still used by long-lived operator creds) and improve post-facto auditability for region-pinned KMS calls. Changes include: - RBAC revocation webhook: validates backend grant store for expiry and revocation markers before allowing privileged operator actions. Webhook runs as a scaled service with fast cache and soft-fail fallback policy. - KMS attribution pipeline: captures per-request provenance (principal, grant-id, origin-region, effective-region-pin) and appends structured fields to the audit stream and metrics exporter. - Audit consistency checker: background job that scans recent audit events and flags any KMS call that lacks valid grant evidence or used a non-pinned region. - Observability: adds rbac.kms_attribution counters, histogram for attribution_latency_ms, and alert rules for attribution_mismatch_rate. - Docs and rollout: docs/security/rbacv2-revocation-webhook.md, console alert, and helm values for staged rollout. Design notes and constraints: webhook uses a read-through cache keyed by (grant-id, principal) with TTL tuned for low-latency reads; on cache miss it performs a strongly consistent lookup to grant store. Soft-fail policy: in regions with intermittent grant-store connectivity, webhook can be configured to 'audit-only' to avoid blocking users while still surfacing violations. KMS attributor attaches a signed provenance header to outbound KMS calls when running in Private/Dedicated modes; hosted mode emits attribution to the audit log only. Rollout plan: - Phase 1: shadow webhook in canary cluster (2/15-2/18) - Phase 2: enable enforcement for internal operator roles (2/19) - Phase 3: enable enforcement for tenant-scoped operator tokens with telemetry gating (2/20) Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for webhook cache and decision paths - [x] Integration test covering expired grant rejection - [x] End-to-end test for KMS attribution header and audit ingestion - [x] Docs updated and reviewed - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Security scan passed Related: ENG-9123 (design), SUP-4219 (customer escalations).
commits: feat(rbac): add temporal revocation webhook + cache and basic decision API
feat(kms): add attribution middleware and signed provenance header for private/dedicated
test: add integration tests for expired grant rejection and kms attribution ingestion
docs: rbacv2 revocation webhook usage and rollout notes
observability: add metrics and alert rules for attribution_mismatch_rate
chore: helm chart values and deploy script for staged rollout
fix(test): address race in grant-store mock used by integration tests
review_comments: Drew Kaplan: Nice work. Two things: (1) can we expose a metric for cache_miss_rate so SRE can tune TTL? (2) add a note about fallback semantics when grant-store is unreachable.
Aisha Patel: Added cache_miss_rate metric and documented fallback policy in the design notes. Also added a helm flag 'enforcer.auditOnlyOnGrantStoreFailure' to control soft-fail behavior.
Ravi Menon: Integration test looks good but saw a flake when running under godev: CI failed once for the grant-store mock - please make the mock deterministic.
Aisha Patel: Fixed mock determinism and added retry boundary for test harness. Re-ran CI.
Evelyn Zhou: Security review: verified the provenance header is HMAC-signed with service key and that hosted mode avoids embedding secrets. Approved after addressing token scope comment.
release_notes: Adds RBAC v2 revocation webhook, region-pinned KMS usage attribution, audit consistency checks, and related metrics/alerts. Rollout via helm values with audit-only fallback; no breaking API changes.
